This state needs to be implemented in all of the 7 platforms, and I can't compile and test them all.  Each one has different issues.


Take the Web case, for example.

The `AudioDriverWeb::input_start()` doesn't set any state detectable in the C++ to tell whether it has been called or not.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7ed0b6167618f9c8c5df87c7e83da6003c081368/platform/web/audio_driver_web.cpp#L192

Instead, the state that it is running is known deeper in the Javascript implementation on this line here.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7ed0b6167618f9c8c5df87c7e83da6003c081368/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_audio.js#L1291

There are similar issues with the other platforms, and I am likely to cause bugs.  So the simplest way is to use this global flag to prevent double calls (which are not protected for pulseaudio till this PR is made), and then replace it by the internal state of each platform in the future.
Alright. Yea, no need to add anything new to the driver if they don't have code to handle this yet. The boolean is fine.

Nice idea, but not in common use for buffers.  Buffer gets returning empty or incomplete values when there's not enough data is normally assumed.

For example:

https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_fileaccess.html#class-fileaccess-method-get-buffer

https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_audioeffectcapture.html#class-audioeffectcapture-method-get-buffer
Ok, if it's consistent with current APIs, the current naming is fine with me!

I'm modelling it closely with other functions nobody has an issue with.  It's clarified by the documentation as well as the return value.  I believe my current name will raise fewer objections with people.  If you are think I'm wrong about this I'll change it.

https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_audioeffectcapture.html#class-audioeffectcapture-method-get-frames-available
Thanks for linking the other API. I may disagree with the naming, but it's more important that it's consistent. So your name is fine I think.

Originally I did use `Vector<int32_t>&`, but  @lyuma was adamant that this made things worse because the Vector class contains a CowData array, so it's not being copied if nothing is written. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7ed0b6167618f9c8c5df87c7e83da6003c081368/core/templates/cowdata.h
The data is not copied, but copying Vector still incurs overhead from the atomic. It's better to avoid it when possible.
Common way of doing things.  At least it's not "unsigned int" which is even more strictly true, but has caused me really nasty bugs in the past, so I never use it.

The use of the `ERR_FAIL_COND_V` macro in the init function bails out early and potentially leaves various components of the input driver in an unclean state.  The `input_stop` function needs to be rewritten to clean up these bits of leftover state.  
 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/platform/android/audio_driver_opensl.cpp#L201
Common way for the audio code to use a smaller type? I'm not sure I understand what you mean

While it's true that CowData has `typedef int64_t Size`, almost everywhere I look in the code where the value of a `Vector<X>::size()` is stored to a variable it is of type `int`, so I assume this is normal practice.  There is zero chance that this buffer size overflows 32 bits, or whatever an `int` is.

eg
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/scene/debugger/scene_debugger.cpp#L2706

I'd say to not use old code that's formally incorrect as a guideline, it's better to be safe

The reason there's so many `int` is because `CowData` *used* to be 32 bit until just last year so it's recent so a lot of left over code that wasn't migrated

Adding this if-statement would remove a feature from the engine where it is possible to change the microphone input_device while it is running.  

Instead you would have to call `set_input_device_active(false)`, then change the device, before calling `set_input_device_active(true)`.

This is actually how it is implemented under the hood on some of the platforms, see here:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/drivers/pulseaudio/audio_driver_pulseaudio.cpp#L557

However, this hot-swapping feature is hacky because it handles the case where the new_input_device fails by shutting down the thread, while being unable to inform the game that it has failed.

If changing the input device was only possible when the input was switched off (easy to do with the new function), then the failure case can be properly handled when it is switched back on when `set_input_device_active(true)` is called.

Makes sense.
I think this is worth addressing, but I'd say this is out of scope for the PR. I'd rather do it in a separate PR.

p400 of [the specifications](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenSL-ES/specs/OpenSL_ES_Specification_1.1.pdf) says there is no precondition on the state when calling this function.

Why did the errors checks were removed? I understand that we want to return OK even if the driver wasn't recording, but removing every error check doesn't help either.

It is not useful for `input_stop()` to have an error condition, because you couldn't assume anything (is the input still running?). I've written this function to clean up the incomplete states `init_input_device()` could leave the classes in with its heavy use of the `ERR_FAIL_COND_V` macro to quit early. For these three specific functions [the docs say](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenSL-ES/specs/OpenSL_ES_Specification_1.1.pdf): 1. The only possible error for `SetRecordState()` is `SL_RESULT_PARAMETER_INVALID`, which we can rule out. 2. `SLBufferQueueItf::Clear()` has no error case 3. Destroy() has no return value.

It would be possible to collect the errors and return them at the end, after making sure as much as possible is cleaned up.
Anyway, I agree with Julian that for now trying to clean up as much as possible is preferable to exiting early and leaving behind a broken state. We can try to make this even more robust later. Edit: Or not, if there's no error state to begin with!
